models_evaluated: ResNet-based multi-label deep learning ankle fracture classifier (AO/OTA 2018)

links.outcome: Model AUC on external site data versus internal validation data
links.effect: Fracture detection AUC 0.86 (0.82-0.89) in external set vs 0.95 (0.94-0.97) internal; weighted AUC 0.82 vs 0.93, revealing an external performance gap.
links.quote: Notable was that fracture detection (fracture “yes”/”no”) had AUC 0.86 (0.82–0.89) for the EVD vs. AUC 0.95 (0.94–0.97) for the IVD.

links.outcome: Differences between development and external site datasets and effect on performance
links.effect: External set had three times more type A fractures, fewer views (3 vs 4+), no casts/implants, follow-up images; performance lower externally.
links.quote: In this study, the Flinders data has a different distribution and priori probabilities than the training data.

links.outcome: Effect of active learning with targeted local-like training data on external performance
links.effect: After active learning, external wAUC rose by 0.06 (0.77 to 0.83) and wAUPR from 0.57 to 0.63; group C2 AUPR dropped by 0.40.
links.quote: The wAUC increased by 0.06 (0.77 to 0.83), and the wAUPR increased from 0.57 to 0.63 for the EVD.

links.outcome: Model performance at an external site versus developer's internal site
links.effect: External wAUC 0.86 vs 0.95 internal for fracture detection; type A fractures had lowest AUC and several outcomes did not beat random AUPR.
links.quote: The direct clinical implications of this study are that algorithms developed elsewhere need local validation and that discrepancies can be rectified using targeted training.

links.outcome: Performance variation between two hospital sites
links.effect: wAUC 0.95 internal (Danderyd) vs 0.86 external (Flinders) for fracture detection; different results expected at other hospitals.
links.quote: Compared to the weighted mean AUC (wAUC) 0.86 (95%CI 0.82-0.89) for fracture detection in the EVD, the network attained wAUC 0.95 (95%CI 0.94-0.97) for the IVD.

unlisted_practices: Active learning with uncertainty-based case selection to improve external validity

screen.reason: This is an external validation study of a deep-learning model for ankle fracture classification across two distinct institutional cohorts. While it discusses the importance of local validation, it evaluates model accuracy rather than testing a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
